title: Starting System Specifications — 3.7L Duratec
introduction:
I keep the starter’s effort separate from its result: current draw describes electrical demand, and cranking speed describes engine rotation. Read the row label before the figure, keeping its units attached. The no-load, normal-load and maximum-load current rows cover different conditions. Treating the maximum as everyday demand would give this comparison a very crooked yardstick.

The cranking-speed, no-load-current and normal-load-current figures are labelled as averages. The starting-circuit voltage-drop entry also carries an average label and applies with the engine at normal operating temperature. Voltage drop is voltage used across a circuit section while current flows; an excessive drop can expose resistance that a no-load check misses.

This is a specification reference. Equipment, connection points, measurement timing and diagnostic branches belong to the matching engine test instructions. The table alone does not identify a failed component.

edits.text: Cranking Speed and Starter Electrical Specifications
edits.why: Load state, temperature and average labels are part of the specification. Keeping them attached prevents a measurement taken under one condition from being judged against an unrelated row.
